span.label: mechanisms
span.term: design alternatives are chosen by asking two stated questions about UNDERSTANDABILITY - how hard is each to explain, and how easily can a reader completely grasp it and its implications - and the authors state plainly that this analysis is highly subjective
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the first technique is problem decomposition: the problem is divided into pieces that can be solved, explained AND understood relatively independently, and the paper names the four it used
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the second technique reduces the STATE SPACE rather than the code - fewer states to consider, more coherence, nondeterminism removed where possible - and it is made concrete by two rules about what logs are not allowed to do
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: NONDETERMINISM IS DELIBERATELY ADDED WHERE IT SHRINKS THE STATE SPACE: randomised approaches handle all possible choices in one fashion - choose any, it does not matter - so randomisation is used to simplify leader election even though the general policy was to eliminate it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the comparison is a within-subject crossover: every participant learns both algorithms and takes both quizzes, with the ORDER reversed for about half of them, so that individual differences and the experience gained from the first half are both accounted for
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the two ways the experiment FAVOURED THE COMPETITOR are stated by the authors rather than left to a reader: some participants had prior experience with the rival algorithm, and the rival's teaching video was longer
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the regression model's estimate of the quiz effect is reported as LARGER than the raw score difference, and the gap between the two is explained by prior experience with the rival algorithm rather than set aside
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the participants' own preference is collected AND THEN DISCOUNTED by the authors, who name both reasons it may be unreliable: self-report against measured scores, and the participants' possible knowledge of the hypothesis being tested
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the correctness argument is anchored to a formal specification that is itself the subject of the proof, and the paper states exactly how far the mechanisation reaches - one property mechanically proven, resting on invariants that have not been mechanically checked
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The participants' self-reported preference for Raft may be unreliable and biased by knowledge of the authors' hypothesis

span.label: Raft's strong-leader design rules out some performance optimisations available to leaderless algorithms
span.note: what this limits: the performance comparison: Raft's strong-leader design rules out optimisations available to leaderless algorithms

span.label: Optimisations known for other consensus algorithms were not applied or evaluated here
span.note: what this limits: any performance comparison against optimised implementations: VARIOUS OPTIMIZATIONS HAVE BEEN PROPOSED IN THE LITERATURE FOR OTHER ALGORITHMS; MANY OF THESE COULD BE APPLIED TO RAFT, BUT WE LEAVE THIS TO FUTURE WORK
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The design criterion the paper is built around is the authors' own judgement about how hard things are to explain.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that this algorithm is more understandable by design: the alternatives were judged by how hard each is to explain and how easy it would be for a reader to understand, which are the authors' own assessments
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The understandability result is a quiz given to students on two named courses.
span.note: what this limits: the finding that this algorithm is more understandable than Paxos: it was measured by an experimental study using upper-level undergraduate and graduate students in an Advanced Operating Systems course at Stanford and a distributed computing course elsewhere
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The equivalence claimed with the algorithm it replaces is on result and efficiency, with the structure explicitly different.
span.note: what this limits: treating results about Paxos as results about this algorithm: the paper states it produces an equivalent result and is as efficient, but that its structure is different
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Removing nondeterminism was the general aim, and the paper records where that aim was abandoned.
span.note: what this limits: a description of this algorithm as deterministic by design: the authors state that although they tried in most cases to eliminate nondeterminism, in some situations nondeterminism actually improves understandability
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: counterbalancing the order of the Paxos and Raft portions of the study, half the participants each way
span.note: eliminates: that the difference in quiz scores reflects individual differences in ability or learning carried over from whichever algorithm was studied first, rather than the algorithms' understandability · outcome: held

span.note: about this quote: EXTRACTION, NOT THE PAPER: the quote as extracted ended `and s t n a p c i t r a p`, which is `participants` reversed. It runs on into `i f o r e b m u n` (`number of` reversed) - together the rotated y-axis label of Figure 15, which the extractor read bottom-to-top and placed inside this sentence. The sentence resumes 250 characters later at `the order in which they learned the algorithms`, so the true third factor is the learning order. The quote is TRIMMED rather than mended: joining the two halves would produce a string that reads correctly and exists in no document. Found by TOOLS/find_reversed_figure_text.py; this was the only live quote in the corpus reaching into such a region.
